THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO ISSUE APPROPRIATE WRIT OR ORDER OR DIRECTION AS THE CASE MAY BE AND AWARD COMPENSATION WITH INTEREST FOR THE DEATH OF M.S. KRISHNA MURTHY THE EARNING MEMBER OF THE FAMILY OF THE PETITIONER AND THE RESPONDENTS HAVE LIABLE TO PAY THE COMPENSATION AS PER ANNEXURE-J REPRESENTATION, THROUGH THE LEGAL NOTICE DATED 18.04.2016.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners have sought for a appropriate writ to award compensation for the death of Mr.
M.S.Krishna Murthy, due to electrocution on 03.08.2014.

2. The petitioners claim to be the dependent legal heirs of Mr. M.S.Krishnamurthy and they claim that on 03.08.2014 at about 11:15 a.m., when he was walking near NC: 2023:KHC:33601 Kadrenahalli Circle in Banashankari 2nd stage, he came in contact with a live electric wire and died instantaneously due to the electric shock.
A complaint in that regard was registered by petitioner No.1 with the Banashankari police station on 04.08.2014.

A spot mahazar was drawn by the police as per Annexure-B which disclose that the incident happened, when the deceased was walking near Kadrenahalli in Banashankari 2nd stage and he came in contact with a live electric wire.
A postmortem was conducted on 04.08.2014 which too indicated that the deceased had suffered electric burns and disclosed the entry and exit marks.
A case was registered by the jurisdictional police in Cr.No.194/2011 for an offence punishable under Section 304A of Indian Penal Code and a charge sheet was filed.

In the meanwhile, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 placed the file before the Smt. Veda @ Vedavathi vs The Managing Director on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50479174/
2 Inspectorate of Electricity, Bengaluru South who conducted an investigation and submitted a report on 18.03.2015 to the Principal Secretary, Department of Energy indicating therein that the death of M.S.Krishnamurthy could have been avoided, if the respondent No.3 had taken sufficient care to insulate the electric connection to the street light and accused the NC: 2023:KHC:33601 contractor of respondent No.3 of negligence resulting in death of M.S.Krishnamurthy.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners are therefore before this Court contending that the death of M.S.Krishnamurthy due to electrocution is not in dispute.

They contend that while respondent Nos.1 and 2 claimed that the incident was due to the negligence on the part of respondent No.3 and its contractor, the respondent No.3 claimed the contrary and claimed that the maintenance of street lights was the responsibility of respondent Nos.1 and 2 and respondent no.3 was not responsible in any way.

3. The petitioners contend that since there is no dispute about the nature of the death of M.S.Krishnamurthy, they are entitled to invoke the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

They relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of M.P.Electricity Board Vs. Shail Kumar and others - (2002) 2 SCC 162.
4.

entities.text: M.P.Electricity Board Vs. Shail Kumar and others - (2002) 2 SCC 162
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 and 2 have filed their statement of objections admitting that Sri. M.S.Krishnamurthy died due to a fatal electrical accident, when he came in contact with a live electric wire feeding NC: 2023:KHC:33601 electricity to a street lamp.
They have contended that respondent No.3 had to maintain and operate the switch to cutoff power supply to the street lights during day time.
However, a electrical wire was used for the make and brake electricity supply switch which lead to the unfortunate incident.
They therefore contended that respondent No.3 is responsible for the incident.

5. Respondent No.3 has also filed the statement of objections contending that the writ petition filed against it, is not maintainable, as there were disputed questions of fact that had to be adjudicated.

It claimed that a guy wire is fastened to electricity distribution RCC pole maintained by respondent Nos.1 and 2 and a street light controller box is installed by BBMP on the distribution pole at a safe height and it is operated every day.

It claimed that it was the responsibility of respondent Nos.1 and 2 to maintain the distribution line, the pole and the guy wire for safe operations and it is contended that guy wire shall always be of neutral polarity and if the deceased had come in contact with the guy wire and electrocuted, it is the responsibility of the respondent Nos.1 and 2.
NC: 2023:KHC:33601 6.
Learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 and 2 has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Himachal Pradesh and Ors.
Vs. Naval Kumar Alias Rohit Kumar - Civil No.1339/2017 dated 02.02.2017 and contended that it is the State Government which is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
7. I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 to 3.

sentences.text: The fact that the deceased M.S.Krishnamurthy died in an electric accident on 03.08.2014 is admitted by respondent Nos.1 and 2 and not seriously disputed by respondent No.3.
The fact that the deceased was aged 49 years old, is evident from the spot inspection report conducted by the jurisdictional police.
The petitioners claimed that the deceased was employed as a Cook in a hotel and was earning Rs.800/- per day.

As rightly contended by learned counsel for the petitioners, since there is no disputed question of fact involved and as the respondents being instrumentalities of State, this petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is maintainable.

The NC:
2023:KHC:33601 finding of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of M.P.Electricity Board Vs. Shail Kumari and others - (2002) 2 SCC 162 is apposite and relevant paragraph Nos.8 and 13 reads as under:
"8.

entities.text: M.P.Electricity Board Vs. Shail Kumari and others - (2002) 2 SCC 162
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even assuming that all such measures have been adopted, a person undertaking an activity involving hazardous or risky exposure to human life, is liable under law of torts to compensate for the injury suffered by any other person, irrespective of any negligence or carelessness on the part of the managers of such undertakings.
The basis of such liability is the foreseeable risk inherent in the very nature of such activity.
The liability cast on such person is known, in law, as "strict liability".

It differs from the liability which arises on account of the negligence or fault in this way i.e. the concept of negligence comprehends that the foreseeable harm could be avoided by taking reasonable precautions.
If the defendant did all that which could be done for avoiding the harm he cannot be held liable when the action is based on any negligence attributed.
But such consideration is not relevant in cases of strict liability where the defendant is held liable irrespective of whether he could have avoided the particular harm by taking precautions.

13. In the present case, the Board made an endeavour to rely on the exception to the rule of strict NC: 2023:KHC:33601 liability (Rylands v. Fletcher - 1868 3 HL 330)
being "an act of stranger".

The said exception is not available to the Board as the act attributed to the third respondent should reasonably have been anticipated or at any rate its consequences should have been prevented by the appellant-Board.
In Northwestern Utilities Ltd. v. London Guarantee and Accident Co. Ltd. - 1936 AC 108 the Privy Council repelled the contention of the defendant based on the aforecited exception.

entities.text: Northwestern Utilities Ltd. v. London Guarantee and Accident Co. Ltd. - 1936 AC 108
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that case a hotel belonging to the plaintiffs was destroyed in a fire caused by the escape and ignition of natural gas.

The gas had percolated into the hotel basement from a fractured welded joint in an intermediate pressure main situated below the street level and belonging to the defendants which was a public utility company.
The fracture was caused during the construction involving underground work by a third party.

The Privy Council held that the risk involved in the operation undertaken by the defendant was so great that a high-degree care was expected of him since the defendant ought to have appreciated the possibility of such a leakage."
9.

The only issue that needs to be considered is who among the respondents is liable to pay the compensation to the NC: 2023:KHC:33601 petitioners and what is the quantum of compensation to Smt. Veda @ Vedavathi vs The Managing Director on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50479174/
4 be awarded.
10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The fact that Sri. M.S.Krishnamurthy was electrocuted to death on a footpath where the respondent Nos.1 and 2 had erected electricity distribution line is not much in dispute.

Though,
respondent Nos.1 and 2 claimed that the contractor employed by respondent No.3 was negligent in not insulating the switches attached to the street light for making and braking the circuit

,
respondent No.3 contends to the contrary and claims under Section 63 of the Electricity of Act,
2003, it is the responsibility of respondent Nos.1 and 2 to maintain the electrical installation and street lights etc.,
11.

However, the fact remains that the responsibility of providing street light was upon the respondent No.3 and it is the contractor employed by respondent No.3 who had installed the make and brake switch, to switch on and switch off the street light.
Therefore, the respondents have to work out an interdepartmental adjudication as to who is responsible to pay the compensation.

However, insofar as the petitioners are concerned, they are bound to be compensated by the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:33601 respondents jointly and severally as held by High Court of Delhi in the case of Rajeev Singhal and another Vs. Municipal Corporation of Delhi and another - 2019 ACJ 317.

entities.text: Rajeev Singhal and another Vs. Municipal Corporation of Delhi and another - 2019 ACJ 317
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, it is held that the petitioners are entitled to recover compensation from respondents jointly and severally.
12. Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, there is no measure prescribed by the respondent Nos.1 and 2, as to what should be the compensation payable.

However, the Courts have evolved from time to time, the manner of payment of compensation in motor vehicle cases by adopting a multiplier based on method to determine the compensation and taking into consideration the age of the deceased and his avocation, etc.
Consequently, the same could be borrowed to tentatively determine the compensation payable to the petitioners so as to provide them succor due to loss of a bread earner in the family.
13. Compensation that may be awarded by this Court shall be treated as tentative and shall not be the final compensation payable to the petitioners.

In that view of the matter, this Court considers it appropriate to consider the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.8,500/- per month and also to factor 25% towards loss of future prospects.
The deceased was 49 years old and therefore, the proper multiplier would be '13'.
Out of the notional income, 1/4th of the same deserves to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
Consequently, the total compensation payable would be Rs.12,43,164/-.

(8,500 + 25% = 10,625 - 25% =7969) (Rs.7,969/- x 12 x 13) Petitioner No.1 has lost consortium of the deceased while petitioner Nos.2 and 3 have lost the parental love and affection, while petitioner No.4 has lost filial love and affection consequently, they are entitled to an additional sum of Smt. Veda @ Vedavathi vs The Managing Director on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50479174/
5 Rs.1,60,000/- towards loss of love and affection and a sum of Rs.70,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses etc.,

entities.text: Veda @ Vedavathi vs The Managing Director
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that view of the matter, the total compensation payable would be Rs.14,73,164/-.
Petitioners are entitled to recover a sum of Rs.14,73,164/- from the respondents jointly and severally along with interest @ 8% interest from the 03.08.2014 till the date of realization.
It is made clear that the petitioners are entitled to file appropriate suit for recovery of any further compensation, if they are so advised.
Office is directed to draw an award in the form prescribed for an award under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,1988.
